title: The First Lie
description: A clean starter mystery built around one missing allergy marker, one switched drink, and one suspect whose statement cannot survive Forensics.

answerKey.method: She switched Lena’s allergy-safe marked drink with an unmarked praline cocktail after moving the blue allergy pick.
answerKey.motive: She feared Lena would replace her as lead event bartender.
answerKey.keyEvidence: Forensics connects the missing blue allergy pick, guest photo sequence, register camera still, and Tessa’s own text.
answerKey.explanation: Tessa knew Lena’s allergy marker system, confirmed the blue pick mattered in her text, and was alone at the service rail during the window when the safe glass became unmarked.

phone.title: Recovered Phone Analysis: Drink Pickup Window
phone.text: Lena’s recovered phone stayed near the host table until 8:47 PM, then moved toward the service rail immediately before the collapse.
phone.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

messages.title: Message Extraction Report: Blue Marker Text
messages.text: Tessa texted Lena, “I marked yours blue like always,” confirming that the blue pick was not decoration; it identified Lena’s allergy-safe drink.
messages.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

bank.title: Financial Records Review: Payroll Pressure
bank.text: Tessa had a pending payroll dispute and had been warned that Lena might take over lead bartender duties for future events.
bank.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

photos.title: Photo / Video Review: Marked Glass
photos.text: A guest photo taken before Lena collapsed shows her glass on the service rail with a blue allergy pick inserted through the garnish.
photos.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.
photos.sight: The blue marker is clearly visible above the rim.

photos.title: Photo / Video Review: Marker Missing
photos.text: A second guest image taken after the pickup shows Lena’s glass without the blue allergy pick.
photos.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

social.title: Guest Clip Review: Two Glasses Pulled Together
social.text: A short guest clip catches Tessa pulling two similar glasses together before one leaves the rail.
social.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Tessa Marchand
contacts.text: Tessa says she marked Lena’s glass blue and left it on the rail. She insists the event was too busy for her to track every drink after that.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Owen Landry
contacts.text: Owen says he was at the office door dealing with a sponsor receipt and only looked toward the rail after people started shouting.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Brielle Fox
contacts.text: Brielle says she saw Tessa pull two glasses close together, then heard Tessa snap that the blue marker was “already handled.”

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Cole Darden
contacts.text: Cole says the blue allergy pick was on the garnish tray after Lena collapsed, even though he remembered seeing it in the drink earlier.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Mara Quill
contacts.text: Mara says Tessa had complained that Lena was “getting handed everything” and might take the lead bartender slot.

notes.title: Physical Evidence Report: Garnish Tray
notes.text: The blue allergy pick is recovered from the garnish tray, not from Lena’s glass or table.
notes.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.
notes.physics: The pick is dry, suggesting it was removed before the drink was spilled.

files.title: Document / Metadata Review: Service Rail Still
files.text: The register camera still shows Tessa alone at the service rail for nineteen seconds during the drink pickup window.
files.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.
files.sight: No other staff member is inside the rail frame.

files.title: Final Forensic Summary: Drink Swap Confirmed
files.text: The photo sequence, register still, and recovered garnish tray place the marker change inside Tessa’s service-rail window.
files.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

browser.title: Browser History Review: Termination Policy
browser.text: A recovered staff tablet shows Tessa searched the venue handbook section on termination and lead-shift reassignment that afternoon.
browser.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

openingNarration: Detectives, the crime scene has already been processed. Your job is to read the Forensics reports, test the suspects in Interrogation, place events on the Timeline, and answer each Deduction before the final accusation opens.
revealScript: The case turns on the blue allergy pick. Tessa did not need a complicated weapon; she needed the right glass to become the wrong glass at the right moment. Forensics proved the marker changed, Interrogation exposed her pressure, and the Timeline placed her at the service rail.
